cards.info: What is the definition of a relation in mathematics?
cards.backInfo: A relation is any set of ordered pairs consisting of inputs and outputs.

cards.info: What specific requirement defines a function?
cards.backInfo: A function is a relation where each input corresponds to exactly one output.

cards.info: When does a relation fail to be a function?
cards.backInfo: It fails if a single input is paired with two or more different outputs.

cards.info: What is the first step of the Domain-Output Pair Scan?
cards.backInfo: The first step is to list every distinct input, or domain element, from the relation.
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A flow chart showing the steps to determine if a relation is a function: Identify Inputs, Map to Outputs, Check for Multiple Outputs per Input, and Determine Function Status.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/bb5c49c4-d4fd-4537-b3de-9610064eede2-1786505821105-244.webp)

cards.info: Can multiple inputs share the same output in a function?
cards.backInfo: Yes, multiple inputs can share one output, but one input cannot have multiple outputs.

cards.info: If all x-coordinates are unique, is the relation a function?
cards.backInfo: Yes, if every x-coordinate is unique, the relation is guaranteed to be a function.

cards.info: Is a relation disqualified as a function if y-values repeat?
cards.backInfo: No, it is a mistake to assume repeating y-values disqualify a relation from being a function.

cards.info: How is a non-function identified on a mapping diagram?
cards.backInfo: A relation is not a function if any input has multiple arrows originating from it.

cards.info: Why is the relation {(1, 2), (1, 3)} not a function?
cards.backInfo: It is not a function because the input 1 is associated with two different outputs.

cards.info: How do you verify a function using a table of values?
cards.backInfo: Ensure that every time an x-value repeats, the corresponding y-value is identical.

cards.info: What components make up the ordered pairs in a mathematical relation?
cards.backInfo: A relation consists of sets of inputs (x-values) and outputs (y-values).

cards.info: In a function, how many outputs can a single domain element have?
cards.backInfo: Each domain element (input) must correspond to exactly one output.

cards.info: Does the relation {(5, 2), (5, 4)} qualify as a function?
cards.backInfo: No, because the single input 5 is paired with two different outputs.

cards.info: What must you identify before mapping outputs in the Domain-Output Pair Scan?
cards.backInfo: You must first list every distinct input or domain element in the relation.
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A flow chart showing the steps to determine if a relation is a function: Identify Inputs, Map to Outputs, Check for Multiple Outputs per Input, and Determine Function Status.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/bb5c49c4-d4fd-4537-b3de-9610064eede2-1786505821105-244.webp)

cards.info: Compare input/output uniqueness requirements for a valid function.
cards.backInfo: Inputs can share outputs, but one input cannot map to multiple outputs.

cards.info: What is the fastest way to confirm a set of pairs is a function?
cards.backInfo: Scan the x-coordinates; if they are all unique, it is a function.

cards.info: Is {(1, 7), (2, 7), (3, 7)} a function despite the repeating 7?
cards.backInfo: Yes, repeating y-values are allowed as long as each x-value has one output.

cards.info: What visual cue in a mapping diagram indicates a relation is NOT a function?
cards.backInfo: A single input value having two or more arrows originating from it.

cards.info: What is the final verification step to ensure a relation is a function?
cards.backInfo: Confirm that no domain element appears with two or more different outputs.
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A flow chart showing the steps to determine if a relation is a function: Identify Inputs, Map to Outputs, Check for Multiple Outputs per Input, and Determine Function Status.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/bb5c49c4-d4fd-4537-b3de-9610064eede2-1786505821105-244.webp)

cards.info: Why does the set {(1, 2), (1, 3)} fail the function test?
cards.backInfo: The input 1 maps to two different outputs (2 and 3) simultaneously.
